newsitem.title: HAITI: Wanted Haitian politician said to be in New Jersey.
newsitem.headline: Wanted Haitian politician said to be in New Jersey.

text.p: An opposition party leader wanted by Haitian authorities for alleged links to terrorist activities by ex-soldiers left Haiti and moved to New Jersey, Haitian National Police Chief Pierre Denize said on Monday.
"I don't know what means he used to get there," Denize said. He said he did not know where in New Jersey Deronceray was located.
U.S. embassy spokewoman Meg Gilroy said embassy personnel "did not admit having any knowledge" that Hubert DeRonceray, leader of the National Mobilisation for Democracy, was in the United States.
An arrest warrant for DeRonceray was posted after the Aug. 19 attacks by what were believed to be ex-soldiers on the Port-au-Prince police station and parliament building.
The attackers wore military fatigues and threw grenades at the buildings. Haitian officials alleged the attack was planned at an MDN meeting days before.
The day after the attacks Antoine Leroy, the number-two man in the MDN, and party member Jacques Florival were assassinated outside of Florival's home.
Gilroy added that although DeRonceray's wife is a U.S. citizen, she was not sure if he had also been granted citizenship or had a travel visa for the United States.
The U.S. embassy declined to comment on rumours recently circulating in the capital that DeRonceray was receiving asylum in the U.S. embassy.
The Haitian soldiers, disbanded in 1995 at the end of a three-year bloody military coup, threatened violence if their demands for back pay and pensions were not met.
